_note: The cushion and pocket outline (spec 6.3, 7.5, 7.6; physics/table_shape.hpp). Metres, core frame (origin at the table centre, +x to the top cushion, +y to the left seen from baulk); angles in radians from +x towards +y, an arc covering [angle_start, angle_end] anticlockwise (angle_start in [-pi, pi), angle_end may pass pi). 'dimensions' are the design numbers, each with its source in 'docs'; 'lines', 'arcs' and 'pockets' are built from them as 'construction' says, by tools/make_table_shape.py, and the table shape tests check that they still match. Change a dimension only with its source.
construction: Cushion noses ('kind': 'nose') run along the playing area's edges. At each pocket each nose ends in a jaw: a circular arc of jaw_radius_m, tangent to the nose, that turns away from the table through jaw_sweep_rad to the cushion's tip. A corner jaw starts corner_jaw_start_m short of the corner point (where the two nose lines cross); a middle jaw starts middle_jaw_start_m from the pocket's centre line. From each tip a straight facing ('kind': 'facing') runs on along the jaw's tangent until it is level with the far edge of the drop circle, measured along the pocket's axis (the diagonal through the corner point; square to the cushion for a middle pocket). Each drop circle is the hole in the bed: its centre sits on the pocket's axis, corner_drop_centre_m beyond the corner point or middle_drop_centre_m behind the nose line, with the matching drop radius.

playing_length_m.source: WPBSA Official Rules (2022) section 1: 3569 mm between the cushion faces; table_geometry.hpp
playing_length_m.note: The top and baulk cushion noses lie at x = +-length/2.

playing_width_m.source: WPBSA Official Rules (2022) section 1: 1778 mm between the cushion faces; table_geometry.hpp
playing_width_m.note: The side cushion noses lie at y = +-width/2.

jaw_radius_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.corner_side_jaw.radius (the corner and middle jaws agree to 0.01 mm; the arc fits the cushion nose to 0.12 mm).
jaw_radius_m.note: Every jaw is this arc at the cushion's nose height, tangent to the nose line and turning away from the table. The model's cushions curve into the pockets on this long radius; the owner chose its pockets over the tight 1 in knuckles this file had (2026-11-15).

jaw_sweep_rad.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.corner_side_jaw.sweep_rad.
jaw_sweep_rad.note: How far each jaw turns before the cushion ends: 56.4 degrees, leaving the tip 45.2 mm behind the nose line. The facing carries on along the tangent, so a corner pocket widens behind its tips.

corner_jaw_start_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, half_length - outline.corner_side_jaw.start. The model as bought has 87 mm; fit_table.py draws each corner cushion back 16 mm (CORNER_PULL) for the owner's rule that pots must not get harder with the new table (2026-11-15), set by measuring pot widths against the outline this file had before (ofs_sim_cli pots --against).
corner_jaw_start_m.note: Where a corner jaw leaves the nose line, short of the corner point. As bought, the model's corner mouth leaves a 52.5 mm ball 14 mm of play. Drawn back 13 mm it matched the old 84 mm gap head-on but took fewer balls from 30 degrees off the diagonal outwards, because the long round jaws rattle a ball the old knuckles fed in; at 16 mm the mouth is 86 mm at its narrowest and takes at least as many as the old outline at every angle to 30 degrees and at pace along the cushion. A dying ball along the cushion still drops less often than it did.

middle_jaw_start_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, -outline.middle_jaw.start.
middle_jaw_start_m.note: Where a middle jaw leaves the nose line, from the pocket's centre line. The tips end 93 mm apart.

corner_drop_centre_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.corner_fall.centre, taken along the diagonal from the corner point.
corner_drop_centre_m.note: The centre of the hole cut in the bed at a corner. With the radius below, the fall begins 0.5 mm beyond the corner point.

corner_drop_radius_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.corner_fall.radius (the bed's cut, fitted to 0.4 mm).
corner_drop_radius_m.note: A ball drops once its centre is over the hole (spec 7.6).

middle_drop_centre_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.middle_fall.centre, behind the cushion nose line.
middle_drop_centre_m.note: The centre of the hole cut in the bed at a middle pocket. The fall begins 2 mm behind the nose line: the middle pockets are no longer set back.

middle_drop_radius_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.middle_fall.radius (the bed's cut, fitted to 0.2 mm).
middle_drop_radius_m.note: A ball drops once its centre is over the hole (spec 7.6).

rail_width_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.rail_outer_x - half_width.
rail_width_m.note: Cushion nose to the rail's outer edge, for the cue obstruction (spec 7.3).

rail_height_m.source: Measured on the bought table model (Studio-Lab 'Snooker Table', Fab) as fitted to this playing area by tools/fit_table.py: game/licensed/fit.json, outline.rail_top.
rail_height_m.note: Rail top above the cloth, for the cue obstruction (spec 7.3). The cushion's nose is 33 mm above the cloth in the model; the physics keeps its own contact height.
